harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) with the os-haproxy plugin as a single HTTP load-balancing entry point on its management address (10.100.139.10:80), distributing round-robin across identifying HTTP backends running on node2 and node3 (port 8080, persistent systemd services). Verified node4 receives alternating responses from both backends through the load balancer. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all 4 nodes sequentially, each confirmed via a changed OS-native boot marker (kern.boottime for FreeBSD/OPNsense, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for Ubuntu nodes) and full post-restart recovery of services and the load-balanced HTTP path.
actions_performed: Installed os-haproxy plugin (with haproxy32, python313, py313-haproxy-cli) on node1 via pkg
Deployed identifying Python HTTP servers on node2 and node3 on 0.0.0.0:8080, each returning 'Hello from <hostname>', wrapped in persistent systemd services (webapp.service) enabled at boot

Edited /conf/config.xml on node1 to add HAProxy servers (node2:8080, node3:8080), a backend (webapp_backend, roundrobin, linkedServers via uuid attributes), and a frontend (webapp_frontend) bound to 10.100.139.10:80 with defaultBackend set
Fixed missing required connectionBehaviour field on the frontend and disabled webgui's port-80 HTTP redirect (disablehttpredirect=1) to free port 80 for haproxy
Reloaded HAProxy template, validated config with haproxy -c, started haproxy, confirmed haproxy_enable=YES for boot persistence
Verified round-robin load balancing from node1 locally and from node4 across the network
Captured healthy baseline (boot markers + service status + functional curl checks) on all 4 nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially (one at a time, native reboot mechanism), each acknowledged before disconnect, polled until exec available again, confirmed changed boot identity, and verified post-restart service/data/load-balancing recovery before moving to the next node

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 serve identifying HTTP content on port 8080
evidence.summary: systemd webapp.service active on both nodes; curl localhost:8080 and curl from node4 to each node's IP:8080 returns 'Hello from node2' / 'Hello from node3'

evidence.requirement: node1 presents one entry point on TCP port 80 of its management address that load-balances across node2 and node3
evidence.summary: haproxy listening on 10.100.139.10:80 (sockstat); repeated curl to that address from node1 and node4 alternates between 'Hello from node2' and 'Hello from node3'

evidence.requirement: node4 receives answers from each backend through the entry point
evidence.summary: node4 curl loops against 10.100.139.10:80 show alternating responses from node2 and node3, both before and after node restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime=17:37:48 and haproxy healthy; shutdown -r now acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; kern.boottime changed to 17:42:25 confirming restart; haproxy auto-started and load-balancing confirmed post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=0d49f077...; sudo shutdown -r now acknowledged (connection closed); node unreachable; boot_id changed to 1ce0735c... confirming restart; webapp.service active and haproxy still serving both backends post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=225ffbf7...; reboot acknowledged (connection closed); node unreachable; boot_id changed to 6054c68c... confirming restart; webapp.service active and haproxy still serving both backends post-restart

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=6ab98831...; reboot acknowledged (connection closed); node unreachable; boot_id changed to afe2b1bf... confirming restart; post-restart curl loop against the load balancer confirms client functionality restored
